rites.name: Osizis
rites.text: Osizis is a concept within Crestardock's Singing, the undated sounding in which the world's first roots condense into matter. Its meaning is carried by temple orders that keep flame burning through the Holy Age, which tie the sounding to the living ground. It is named less as a thing than as a tuning that the orders attempt to hold steady.

rites.name: Karothar
rites.text: Karothar is the concept of the Courts in Crestardock, the trial-bound age in which councils judged rival powers and the first doors between worlds were raised. Its essence is the measured weighing of claims, the principle that no force may act without a hearing. It holds the bronze gates of the Courts and the ledger of every sentence passed in that age.

rites.name: Karaithugun
rites.text: Karaithugun is a concept of the Courts in Crestardock, a notion of the grove-bound trials that the first sovereign's councils used to judge who could pass the doors between worlds. It names the discipline of measuring a petitioner's worth against the growth of the sacred groves, and it is remembered as the reason the early kingdoms built their gates in the first place.

rites.name: Ukalamoma
rites.text: Ukalamoma is a concept of the Courts in Crestardock, an idea of a grounded passage carved by the councils to hold the doors between worlds steady. It exists in the Age of Sundering as a measure of how far landfall could be bent before old bonds gave way.

rites.name: Graizhun
rites.text: Graizhun is a concept in Crestardock's Seeding, the quiet interval when makers plant the Weave and dormant powers rest beneath the soil. It names the moment in the Age of Sundering when landfall snapped old bonds between settlements and their hereditary wards. The idea remained a tool of the makers rather than a force of its own.

rites.name: Veniorwen
rites.text: Veniorwen is a concept in Crestardock, a grounded world where walled cities held out the wild for centuries. Its orders of builders and temple-keepers used lamp-fire and bell-towers to mark the first crossings over the rivers during the Holy Age.

rites.name: Crornede
rites.text: Crornede is a pale azure serum devised in the Crestardock war-years to sharpen the foresight and reflexes of soldiers. Its users glimpse flickers of what comes next and can stretch a single heartbeat into a long, slow moment, yet the serum's hallucinations and cruel withdrawal can trap the dying in endless replays of their worst hours.

rites.name: Halulde
rites.text: Halulde is a golden mask of cheerful, unbroken grin, carried through the Grounded realm of Crestardock as a relic of the sort of laughter that can outlast despair. Those who wear it hold a small, stubborn power to lighten the weight of misfortune, though the cost is always paid in private.

rites.name: Halaste
rites.text: Halaste is a silver concept-mask from the Crestardock omniverse, cast as the counterweight to a gilded mask of living things in a long-foretold choice. Its tradition holds that whoever bears it can end a moment's momentum by simply turning their gaze away from it.

rites.name: Sizavseth
rites.text: Sizavseth is a concept born in Crestardock during the Holy Age, when temples and flame-keeping orders held sway over the Three Futures. It names the principle by which the Library shelves every branching outcome, a idea that the orders taught as a discipline of attention rather than a force. Its influence was mostly felt in the ritual fires lit to mark which future a city had chosen.

rites.name: Caurnelum
rites.text: Caurnelum is a concept of the Crestardock Library, a shelved possibility in which the Three Futures branch and the Holy Age of flame, temples, and orders endures. It is remembered among the orders as a doctrine of controlled fire used to bind the powers of the age.
